openerRule: Source-neutral DIRECT base, HEARD_OF and DO_YOU_KNOW selectively at #2/#5/#9/#13/#20/#24/#29/#36/#43/#48; no fiction or obligatory bridge.
sourceFidelityGate: Original title mandatory; Power and Lore included in candidate semantics but independent card-by-card editorial critique pending; no 90% claim

source.power: Stasis Loop. Play this to cancel any Quest progression this turn. Narrate why nothing can change.
source.lore: Dysfunction isn't just a state; it's a habit. We normalize the abnormal until the extraordinary seems impossible.

rows.spokenLine: The Ordinary World cancels all Quest progress for a turn and demands an explanation of why nothing can change; dysfunction has become such a habit that the extraordinary seems impossible.

source.power: Cognitive Dissonance. Increase Quest Die by +1. Force another player to introduce a conflict that disrupts their current plans.
source.lore: The universe doesn't knock. It throws a brick. The disruption of normalcy is always the beginning.

rows.spokenLine: Ever heard of The Call to Adventure? Raise the Quest Die by one and make another player introduce a conflict that wrecks their plans; the universe doesn't knock, it throws a brick.

source.power: Rational Panic. Pause the Quest for one turn. All players must explain why they can't possibly go on the adventure.
source.lore: Fear is realistic self-preservation. Change means death of the familiar self. The familiar self is terrible at math.

rows.spokenLine: Refusal of the Call pauses the Quest for one turn so everyone can explain why they can't go; fear calls that self-preservation, and the familiar self is terrible at math.

source.power: External Hard Drive. Draw 2 cards. Give 1 to another player. Wisdom is useless until it's shared.
source.lore: The Mentor cannot go with you. They provide the map, not the legs.

rows.spokenLine: Meeting the Mentor lets you draw two cards and give one away; wisdom only works when shared, because the Mentor gives you the map, not the legs.

source.power: Point of No Return. Move Quest Die +2. Discard your hand and draw 3 new cards. The old world is gone.
source.lore: Commitment is the moment fear becomes movement. You can't un-take the step.

rows.spokenLine: Do you know Crossing the Threshold? Move the Quest Die two forward, discard your hand and draw three; the old world is gone, because commitment makes fear into movement and you cannot un-take the step.

source.power: Digestion. All players discard 1 card. No Quest progress this turn. Next turn, the Quest Die doubles.
source.lore: Liminal space. No longer who you were, not yet who you'll become.

rows.spokenLine: Belly of the Whale makes everybody discard a card and suspends Quest progress for a turn before doubling the Quest Die; you're no longer who you were and not yet who you'll become.

source.power: Grindset. Narrate 3 small problems. For each one you 'solve' in the fiction, gain +1 to your next roll.
source.lore: Recovery is practice. The hero who survives the trials is not the hero who entered them.

rows.spokenLine: Road of Trials asks for three small problems, adding one to your next roll for every fictional solution; recovery is practice, and the survivor isn't the hero who started.

source.power: Self-Love Bomb. Narrate a moment of acceptance. Quest Die +1 for every player who agrees you deserve it.
source.lore: The experience of being fully seen. The internal integration of opposites into unconditional love.

rows.spokenLine: Meeting the Goddess asks you to narrate acceptance and adds one to the Quest Die for every player who agrees you deserve it; being fully seen means accepting the opposites within.

source.power: Regression Pull. Tempt another player to discard a 'Safety' card. If they do, they gain a reward but lose 2 on the Quest Die.
source.lore: The siren song of comfort. The familiar cage feels safer than the unknown field.

rows.spokenLine: Ever heard of Woman as Temptress? Tempt another player to discard a Safety card for a reward, but take two off the Quest Die; the familiar cage feels safer than the unknown field.

source.power: Daddy Issues. Identify an Authority Card on the Stage. Destroy it or Integrate it. Both options work differently.
source.lore: Confront the source of authority. Kill the internal 'should' to find the authentic 'want.'

rows.spokenLine: Atonement with the Father confronts an Authority card: destroy it or integrate it, with different results; to find the authentic 'want,' you must face the internal 'should.'

source.power: Ego Death. Discard your Actor Marker. You are now a Formlessness. You may intervene in any scene as a nameless force.
source.lore: The caterpillar is liquid. The butterfly is inevitable.

rows.spokenLine: Apotheosis discards your Actor Marker and lets you intervene in any scene as a nameless force; the caterpillar is liquid, and the butterfly is inevitable.

source.power: The Elixir. Gain a permanent 'Treasure' token. Use it once to auto-succeed on any Quest roll.
source.lore: Integration of the lesson. It's not the object, it's the internal shift the object represents.

rows.spokenLine: The Ultimate Boon gives you a permanent Treasure token for one automatic Quest success; the Elixir isn't the object but the internal shift it represents.

source.power: Stay in Narnia. You may choose to end the game for your Actor here. They do not return. They transcend.
source.lore: Why go back to the mundane when you've touched the transcendent? The ordinary world is terrible by comparison.

rows.spokenLine: Do you know Refusal of the Return? Your Actor may end the game without coming back; after touching the transcendent, the ordinary world looks terrible by comparison.

source.power: Escape Velocity. End the Quest immediately. Roll a D6. Even: You keep the Boon. Odd: The Boon is lost in transit.
source.lore: Old patterns don't release easily. The ego will chase you to the threshold.

rows.spokenLine: The Magic Flight ends the Quest and rolls a die: even keeps the Boon, odd loses it in transit; old patterns won't release you, and the ego follows to the threshold.

source.power: Intervention. Play this on another player who is stuck. You automatically provide the next card they need.
source.lore: You can't do it all alone. Community is necessary. Independence is a trauma response.

rows.spokenLine: Rescue from Without supplies a stuck player with the next card they need automatically; you cannot do it alone, because community matters and independence can be a trauma response.

source.power: Re-Entry Shock. Draw 1 card for yourself, give 1 to a neighbor. The gift must be explained in character.
source.lore: The hardest stage. Can you maintain your transformation while re-entering the old context?

rows.spokenLine: Crossing the Return Threshold gives one drawn card to you and another to a neighbor, with the gift explained in character; the hard part is staying changed back in the old context.

source.power: Code Switch. You may play cards from the Discard Pile as if they were in your hand for this turn.
source.lore: No split between 'spiritual' and 'mundane.' You are whole. You are both.

rows.spokenLine: Master of Two Worlds plays cards from the Discard Pile as though they're in your hand; spiritual and mundane no longer split you, because you're both.

source.power: Zen Mode. Your Actor becomes a Mentor. You cannot lose. You just vibe.
source.lore: Freedom from the tyranny of fear. You're alive. That's enough.

rows.spokenLine: Freedom to Live turns your Actor into a Mentor who cannot lose and can just vibe; free of the tyranny of fear, you're alive and that's enough.

source.power: Tragedy of Stagnation. Cancel a 'Call to Adventure.' Nothing happens. The story ends before it begins.
source.lore: Many refuse the call until they die. This is not a moral failure, it is a statistical reality.

rows.spokenLine: The Anti-Journey cancels a Call to Adventure so nothing happens and the story ends before it begins; refusing the call until death isn't a moral failure, just a statistical reality.

source.power: Eternal Recurrence. Reset the Quest Die to [3]. Start the exact same story over, but you know it now.
source.lore: The spiral goes up. Or down. But it definitely goes around.

rows.spokenLine: Ever heard of The Circular Journey? Reset the Quest Die to three and start exactly the same story with the knowledge you kept; the spiral goes up or down, but it definitely goes around.

source.power: Main Character Energy. You may re-roll the Quest Die once per turn.
source.lore: The one who transforms. The ego vehicle. Often confused, usually earnest, always the protagonist.

rows.spokenLine: The Hero rerolls the Quest Die once each turn; the transforming ego vehicle is often confused, usually earnest and always sure it's the main character.

source.power: Projection. Force another player to face a negative consequence you were supposed to face.
source.lore: The dark mirror. The antagonist is just the part of you that you haven't accepted yet.

rows.spokenLine: The Shadow makes another player face the negative consequence meant for you; the antagonist is the part of yourself you haven't accepted yet.

source.power: Trust Issues. Change the 'Suit' or 'Type' of any card on the Stage.
source.lore: Loyalty is ambiguous. Keeps the hero off-balance. Is it love or is it strategy?

rows.spokenLine: The Shapeshifter changes the Suit or Type of a card on Stage; with loyalty this ambiguous, is it love or strategy?

source.power: Wake Up Call. Play immediately when a Quest ends to start a new one automatically.
source.lore: Brings the Call. The Inciting Incident personified. Annoying, but structurally necessary.

rows.spokenLine: Do you know The Herald? It automatically starts a fresh Quest when the last one ends; this Wake Up Call is annoying, but structurally necessary.

source.power: Gatekeeping. Block a player from playing a card on the Stage unless they justify it in character.
source.lore: Tests the hero's resolve. If you can't get past the doorman, you don't get in.

rows.spokenLine: Threshold Guardian blocks another player's Stage card until they justify it in character; if you can't get past the doorman, you don't get in.

source.power: Chaos Agent. Swap the hands of two players. Laugh.
source.lore: Disrupts the status quo. Reveals truth through absurdity. Also, very annoying at parties.

rows.spokenLine: The Trickster swaps the hands of two players and laughs; chaos upsets the status quo, reveals truth through absurdity and gets very annoying at parties.

source.power: Emotional Support. Add +1 to any die roll made by another player.
source.lore: You need a Samwise. Someone to carry the load when you can't.

rows.spokenLine: The Ally adds one to someone else's die roll; everyone needs a Samwise to carry the load when they can't.

source.power: The Bad Ending. Collapse the Quest immediately. No one gets a Boon.
source.lore: The Ordeal can break you. Trauma can win. Not all stories have happy endings.

rows.spokenLine: The Failed Journey collapses the Quest so nobody gets a Boon; an ordeal can break you, trauma can win and not every story gets a happy ending.

source.power: Pressure Cooker. Use this card to set the limits [1] and [6]. If it tips, the reality breaks.
source.lore: Chaos is a valid game state. If the die tips, the reality breaks.

rows.spokenLine: Ever heard of Quest Die? Set its limits to one and six; if the die tips, reality breaks, because chaos is a valid game state.

source.power: Nonsense Check. Play anytime. Force the narrator to pause, clarify, and fix a logic failure. Then laugh.
source.lore: 'It is not an accusation. It is a reset button. Laughter breaks nothing.'

rows.spokenLine: BLÖDSINN! stops the narrator to clarify and fix a logic failure, then laugh; it's a reset button, not an accusation, and laughter breaks nothing.

source.power: Suspension of Disbelief. Treat a lie as truth for the rest of the game.
source.lore: The portrayal of staged events as real. We are all working the gimmick.

rows.spokenLine: Kayfabe treats a lie as truth for the rest of the game; staged events become real when everybody works the gimmick.

source.power: The Author. Change one rule of the game for this turn only.
source.lore: 'I didn't finish this game. That part's yours. Stay fluffy.'

rows.spokenLine: Uncle FrizzleBob can change one game rule for a single turn; he didn't finish this game, because that part's yours.

source.power: Paralysis. You cannot initiate a Quest. You can only react.
source.lore: The cave you fear to enter holds the treasure. But the cave is very dark.

rows.spokenLine: Mood — Fearful stops you from starting a Quest and leaves you only reacting; the cave you fear holds the treasure, but the cave is very dark.

source.power: Leeroy Jenkins. You must play the first card you touch. No thinking allowed.
source.lore: Action without thought. Sometimes it's bravery, sometimes it's a wall.

rows.spokenLine: Mood — Reckless forces you to play the first card you touch without thinking; sometimes that's bravery, sometimes it's a wall.

source.power: Heavy Heart. You cannot win a Boon this turn.
source.lore: Loss is the price of love. The only way out is through.

rows.spokenLine: Mood — Grieving means you cannot win a Boon this turn; loss is the price of love, and the only way out is through.

source.power: Zoomies. Play 2 cards in one turn. Speak twice as fast.
source.lore: Energy without direction. A brilliant disaster.

rows.spokenLine: Do you know Mood — Manic? Play two cards in one turn and speak twice as fast; that's energy without direction, a brilliant disaster.

source.power: Structure. You may rearrange the order of the Scenes on the Stage.
source.lore: 'If it's stupid but it works, it's still stupid, but at least it works.'

rows.spokenLine: Engineering rearranges the Scenes on Stage; if it's stupid but it works, it's still stupid, but at least it works.

source.power: Cut. Remove an unwanted card from the Stage.
source.lore: 'Sometimes the Gordian Knot just needs a sharp edge.'

rows.spokenLine: Swordplay cuts an unwanted card out of the Stage; sometimes the Gordian Knot needs a sharp edge.

source.power: Chill. Prevent a 'Kayfa-BOOM' (Quest Collapse) by negotiating the Die back into safe range.
source.lore: 'The art of telling someone to go to hell in such a way that they look forward to the trip.'

rows.spokenLine: Diplomacy negotiates the Quest Die back into a safe range before Kayfa-BOOM; the art is telling someone to go to hell so nicely they look forward to the trip.

source.power: Yoink. Steal a card from another player's hand.
source.lore: 'Property is theft. Theft is also theft. It's complicated.'

rows.spokenLine: Thievery steals a card from somebody else's hand; property is theft, theft is also theft, and it's complicated.

source.power: Retcon. Undo the last turn completely. It never happened.
source.lore: The past is fluid. Memory is a creative act.

rows.spokenLine: Timeline Shift undoes the last turn completely so it never happened; the past is fluid and memory is a creative act.

source.power: Edit. Change the text on a Quest card.
source.lore: Reality is a draft. Feel free to mark it up.

rows.spokenLine: The Tenth Art edits the text of a Quest card; reality is a draft, so mark it up.

source.power: Parallel Play. Start a second Quest alongside the first one. Run them simultaneously.
source.lore: Why settle for one disaster when you can have infinite disasters?

rows.spokenLine: Ever heard of Multiverse? Start a second Quest alongside the first and run them together; why settle for one disaster when you could have infinite disasters?

source.power: Zoom In. Play a card *inside* another card (place it underneath). It is a story within the story.
source.lore: The spiral goes down. Every story contains a smaller story waiting to unspool.

rows.spokenLine: Fractal Narrative plays one card underneath another, a story inside a story; the spiral goes down, because every story contains a smaller one.

source.power: Decisive Action. +2 to Quest Die. Resolves conflict violently.
source.lore: The symbol of power. Use it to cut the cord.

rows.spokenLine: The Sword adds two to the Quest Die and resolves conflict violently; as a symbol of power, it cuts the cord.

source.power: Reflection. Copy the effect of the last card played.
source.lore: Self-knowledge is the most dangerous weapon of all.

rows.spokenLine: The Mirror copies the last card's effect; self-knowledge is the most dangerous weapon of all.

source.power: Access. Bypass a 'Threshold Guardian' without discarding.
source.lore: Opens doors. Also opens wounds. Be careful.

rows.spokenLine: The Key bypasses a Threshold Guardian without discarding; it opens doors and wounds, so be careful.

source.power: Direction. Look at the top 3 cards of the deck. Arrange them.
source.lore: It doesn't tell you where to go, only where you are.

rows.spokenLine: Do you know The Compass? Peek at the deck's top three cards and arrange them; it won't tell you where to go, only where you are.

source.power: Create. Draw your own artifact here.
source.lore: The map is unfinished. That part's yours.

rows.spokenLine: [BLANK] — 1 lets you draw your own artifact; the map is unfinished and that part is yours.

source.power: Create. Draw your own artifact here.
source.lore: Fill the void before it fills you.

rows.spokenLine: [BLANK] — 2 lets you draw your own artifact; fill the void before it fills you.

source.power: The Judge. Resolve any dispute at the table. Your word is law.
source.lore: Authority as performance. Someone has to wear the crown.

rows.spokenLine: King Kayfabian resolves any table dispute because his word is law; authority is performance, and someone has to wear the crown.

source.power: Game Over. The game ends immediately. Everyone loses? Everyone wins? Scramble the data.
source.lore: They found us. Scramble the data.

rows.spokenLine: The Black Helicopter ends the game immediately and scrambles the data; they found us, and it's not even clear whether everyone loses or wins.

source.power: [INSTRUCTIONS] PRINT on thick paper. CUT along the lines. MIX with your other Kayfabizarro cards.
source.lore: Do not eat the cards. Unless necessary for the plot.

rows.spokenLine: How to Use This Deck says print on thick paper, cut the lines and mix with your other Kayfabizarro cards; don't eat the cards unless the plot requires it.

source.power: [APPROVED BY NOBODY] CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Steal this culture. Remix it. Do not sell it without asking.
source.lore: Copyright is a psyop.

rows.spokenLine: The License says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: remix the culture but ask before selling it; according to the card, copyright is a psyop.

source.power: [SCAN ME] Scan for: Extended Essays, Deep Dives, and The Infinite Backrooms.
source.lore: The truth is online. Or maybe it's a rickroll.

rows.spokenLine: QR Code (Lore) invites you to scan for extended essays, deep dives and Infinite Backrooms; the truth is online, unless it's a rickroll.

source.power: [CARD BACK] Stay Fluffy. / Use this card as a coaster.
source.lore: Stay Fluffy.

rows.spokenLine: Card Back Design prints Stay Fluffy on the back or uses the card as a coaster; either way, Stay Fluffy.
